title: High-Sensitivity Troponin Pathway and Emergency Department Length of Stay
summary: In 16,094 chest-pain encounters across four EDs, a retrospective before-and-after comparison associated an integrated hs-cTn pathway with shorter mean stays: 6.18 hours (95% CI 6.10–6.26) versus 5.64 (5.57–5.71). Serial testing increased from 39.2% to 66.5%.
findings: Mean stay decreased by 0.54 hours; this is an association.
population: Adults with chest pain and troponin testing.
shortTitle: Integrated troponin pathway and ED stay
limitations: Workflow changes, boarding and secular trends confound attribution. Missed MI, readmission and mortality benefits were not established.
whyItMatters: Consider reflex ordering and visible testing status when implementing hs-cTn; an assay change alone may not improve throughput.
evidenceNotes: Primary publisher full text reviewed. Official November 10 release overrides the cache's November 2 hint. Exact-DOI correction search found no relevant notice; absence is not guaranteed. Other pathway trials have mixed throughput findings; do not infer universal benefit.
